problem: Costs had grown and the company wanted to be leaner and flatter.
title: Meta cuts about 21,000 jobs and declares a year of efficiency
context: After heavy hiring and spending, Meta cut about 11,000 jobs in November 2022 and 10,000 more in March 2023.
decision_made: Cut jobs, flatten management and cancel underperforming projects during 2023, framed as a year of efficiency.
action_taken: Announced on the Q4 2022 earnings call and followed with a second round of layoffs.
observed_outcome: Fortune reported that the announcement plus strong first-quarter results sent shares up about 23 percent in one day, and the CEO's wealth rose sharply.
lessons: Cost discipline can be rewarded by investors, but the human cost is large and the stock reaction mixes several causes.
limitations: The 23 percent move combined layoffs and earnings, so cause cannot be separated. The sources do not cover morale, product effects or later hiring.

claims.claim_text: Meta announced a second round of about 10,000 job cuts in March 2023 as part of a year of efficiency.
Fortune linked the efficiency push and strong earnings to a roughly 23 percent one-day share rise.
